title: Noah Lyles wins US 100m championship with world-leading 9.79 seconds
dek: Noah Lyles won the men's 100m at the US athletics championships with a time of 9.79 seconds, the fastest time in the world this year, per BBC Sport.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Noah Lyles ran 9.79 seconds in the men's 100m at the US athletics championships, a world-leading time for 2026.
bottom_line: Lyles' 9.79 secures the US title and marks him as the year's fastest sprinter. Watch for his performances in upcoming international meets to gauge how his form holds against global competition.
body: Noah Lyles won the men's 100m at the US athletics championships with a world-leading time of 9.79 seconds, according to BBC Sport.
Lyles' performance sets the fastest 100m time globally in 2026, positioning him as the frontrunner heading into major international competition.
